content: The information provided here is not a substitute for the advice of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete details about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Erythromycin is a macrolide antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It may also be prescribed to prevent certain bacterial infections. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Erythromycin is typically administered as an injection into a vein, as directed by your doctor, usually every six hours. The injection should be given slowly over 20 to 60 minutes. This injectable form is used only until you can switch to an oral antibiotic or until your treatment is complete. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use it if either is present. For optimal results, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are treating an infection, continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may result in a return of the infection. If you are using this medication to prevent infections, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loose stools, stomach pain, or pain/redness at the injection site. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, erythromycin may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. diff), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using erythromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other macrolide/ketolide antibiotics (e.g., clarithromycin, azithromycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Erythromycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). It may also cause a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation), which can increase the risk of serious irregular heartbeats. The risk of QT prolongation may be higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood may also increase this risk, especially if you are using certain medications (e.g., diuretics) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Infants may be at higher risk for a serious stomach condition. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Erythromycin passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of erythromycin from your body, impacting its effectiveness. Erythromycin can also slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting how they work. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., urine tests), possibly causing false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: Your doctor may order lab or medical tests while you are using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: It is important to receive each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Storage: Consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
